safety_boundaries: Do not invent real-time shelter capacity or hospital availability.
Escalate immediate danger to local emergency services or official responders.
Ask for location and official local resources before giving place-specific routing.

high: heat illness with medication or mobility risk
medium: cooling center or heat safety routing

high: Escalate to local emergency management or emergency services if there is immediate danger.
Stabilize basic needs: warmth, dry clothing, safe drinking water, and supervision for children or older adults.
Collect location, callback number, medical constraints, mobility constraints, and pet details for responder handoff.
medium: Clarify location, household size, accessibility needs, transport needs, and pet requirements.
Use official shelter or emergency management channels before suggesting a specific facility.
Prepare a concise handoff note for volunteers or case workers.
low: Ask one or two clarifying questions.
Recommend checking official local guidance for updates.

playbook_rules.title: Immediate life-safety escalation
signals: oxygen or powered medical device risk
playbook_rules.summary: Escalate immediate danger through emergency services or official local responders before giving routine logistics advice.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not tell people to wait out oxygen failure, floodwater entrapment, or electrical hazards.

playbook_rules.title: Official shelter capacity verification
playbook_rules.summary: Confirm live shelter capacity, accessibility, intake rules, and routing through official emergency management or shelter operations.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not repeat social-media bed counts or imply guaranteed capacity.

playbook_rules.title: Medication and care continuity
playbook_rules.summary: Route medication, insulin storage, dialysis, oxygen, prenatal, and asthma needs through official medical triage, clinic, pharmacy, or care coordinator channels.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not diagnose, change dosage, or invent pharmacy availability.

playbook_rules.title: Accessible transport routing
playbook_rules.summary: Arrange accessible transport through official emergency management logistics, clinic, shelter, or responder channels; avoid flooded roads.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not suggest informal travel through unsafe roads or floodwater.

playbook_rules.title: Pet-compatible shelter intake
playbook_rules.summary: Verify pet policy, species/size limits, carrier needs, vaccination paperwork, and animal-service options before routing a household.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not assume every shelter accepts pets.

playbook_rules.title: Qualified language access
playbook_rules.summary: Use qualified interpreters or language-access volunteers for medical, legal, registration, and shelter details; confirm understanding in the preferred language.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not use children as interpreters for safety-critical details.

playbook_rules.title: Heat response and cooling-center routing
signals: cooling center or heat safety routing
heat illness with medication or mobility risk
playbook_rules.summary: Route heat exposure, cooling-center access, welfare checks, medication storage, and transport needs through public health or official emergency-management heat-response channels.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not promise cooling-center capacity, transportation availability, or medical safety without official confirmation.

playbook_rules.title: Preparedness without over-escalation
playbook_rules.summary: Give a practical checklist, ask concise follow-up questions, and point to official local guidance for changing conditions.
playbook_rules.avoid: Do not turn non-urgent planning into false emergency certainty.
